evidence.content: The document lists common data-quality issues in historical monitoring data, including missing points, single or multiple outliers, stuck values, random or unreasonable values, loss of significant digits and dead band. It recommends identifying such issues before model-based analysis.

The documented incore-excore calibration collects multiple flux distributions during an axial xenon transient, records all excore currents, fits their relationship by linear regression, and adjusts isolation-amplifier gains without changing raw detector current.

The power-range rate circuit compares actual power with a delayed power signal and produces trips for sufficiently high positive or negative rate. The document states that its setpoints are selected so normal design transients do not actuate these rate trips.

The ORNL acquisition chain converted and isolated process current loops, maintained signal and ground isolation, used conditioning with filtering and gain, and simultaneously recorded fourteen channels. Short online analysis during constant-power tests was used to evaluate recording quality.

Once acquired, OLM data can be evaluated and qualified before analysis. Static data qualification addresses the elimination of outliers, spikes, stuck data and noise, and may also include reconstruction of missing data.

The APRM count circuit assesses whether enough LPRM inputs are operable for adequate average-power representation, explicitly accounting for low-range readings that can be zero or near zero.
The report treats redundant-channel averaging and pattern recognition as distinct on-line-monitoring approaches and supplies implementation guidance rather than a single universal method.

The TMI-2 work used noise-analysis methods for several post-accident assessments, including instrumentation performance and bulk coolant boiling; it illustrates diagnostic application scope beyond a single neutron-current channel.
